tagline: Progress Software Corporation enables customers to develop, deploy, and manage responsible AI-powered applications and digital experiences with agility and ease.
hero_kpi_rationale: The company positions itself as a provider of solutions for developing, deploying, and managing AI-integrated applications, which is a key driver in the current technology sector.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total amount of sales of products and services generated by the company.
kpis.description: Total revenue increased by 30% for fiscal year 2025 compared to 2024, primarily due to the acquisition of ShareFile.

kpis.short: Maintenance, SaaS, and Professional Services Revenue
kpis.name: Maintenance, SaaS, and Professional Services Revenue
kpis.explanation: Combined revenue from software maintenance services, SaaS platforms, and consulting services.
kpis.description: This segment, representing the majority of total revenue, saw a significant increase of 47% in 2025, driven by the acquisition of ShareFile.
kpis.signal: Strong growth in recurring and SaaS revenue.

kpis.name: SaaS Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from software platforms delivered as a service (Software-as-a-Service).
kpis.description: SaaS revenue experienced spectacular growth of 546% in 2025, primarily due to the integration of ShareFile.

kpis.name: Software Licenses Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from the sale of traditional software licenses.
kpis.description: Software license revenue declined by 5% in 2025, attributed to the timing of multi-year subscription renewals for the DataDirect offering.
kpis.signal: Slight decline in traditional license revenue.

kpis.short: Cost of Maintenance, SaaS, and Professional Services
kpis.name: Cost of Maintenance, SaaS, and Professional Services
kpis.explanation: Direct expenses related to delivering maintenance, SaaS, and consulting services.
kpis.description: Costs associated with services increased by 48% in 2025, primarily due to increased headcount and hosting costs related to the ShareFile acquisition.
kpis.signal: Cost increase proportional to service revenue growth.

kpis.short: Amortization of Acquired Intangibles - Costs of Revenue
kpis.name: Amortization of Acquired Intangibles - Costs of Revenue
kpis.explanation: Amortization of intangible assets from acquisitions, allocated to cost of revenue.
kpis.description: Amortization of acquired intangible assets increased by 41% in 2025, reflecting recent acquisitions.
kpis.signal: Impact of acquisition-related amortization on costs.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.description: Revenue extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last four reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Revenue of $0.398 Bn in the latest fiscal year (FY2017).

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.description: Net income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last eight reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Net income of $0.073 Bn in the latest fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: ShareFile Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated by ShareFile, acquired in October 2024.
kpis.description: ShareFile contributed $261.6 million in revenue in 2025, following its acquisition in October 2024.
kpis.signal: Significant contribution from a recent acquisition.

kpis.name: MarkLogic Professional Services Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from professional services related to the MarkLogic platform.
kpis.description: MarkLogic professional services declined compared to the prior year.
kpis.signal: Decline in professional services for MarkLogic.

risks.title: Failure of artificial intelligence initiatives
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned early in the 10-K and repeated multiple times with strong language ("adversely affect", "rapidly developing nature"). AI is presented as strategic for the future of products and operations. The Technology category carries high weight in the IT context. Risk level increased compared to the prior year.

risks.title: Dependence on OpenEdge and ShareFile
risks.score_rationale: The document states that these two products represented more than half of revenue in 2025. The language is alarming: "materially adversely affected" if demand declines or new technologies emerge. Central position in the report, with high intensity. Major structural risk.

risks.title: Cyberattacks and security breaches
risks.score_rationale: The risk is detailed across several paragraphs, with mention of an actual incident in 2022 (data exfiltration). Strong language: "significant legal and financial exposure", "damage to reputation". The Cybersecurity category is critical for an IT company. Explicit mention of state-sponsored threats and AI-driven evolution.

risks.title: Increased competition in the software industry
risks.score_rationale: The risk is well-documented, with mention of better-funded and more agile competitors. Language: "intensely competitive", "downward pricing pressure". High placement in the document. Less existential than others as the company has an installed base, but constant pressure.

risks.title: Risks related to acquisitions
risks.score_rationale: The risk is extensively discussed (two pages), with an exhaustive list of post-acquisition threats. Language is highly concerned: "dilution", "unanticipated liabilities", "failure to consummate". Acquisition is a key growth strategy, hence high stakes. Capital category heavily weighted.

risks.title: Dependence on distribution partners
risks.score_rationale: The document emphasizes that a "substantial portion" of revenue flows through third parties (ISVs, resellers, OEMs). Risk of disruption or failure of these partners. Language: "adverse effect on our sales", "not within our direct control". High placement in the text, medium to high intensity.

risks.title: Risks related to international operations
risks.score_rationale: 36% of revenue comes from outside North America. Risks cited: political instability, exchange rates, payment delays. Language is cautious but less alarming than for other risks. Mention of health crises and war, but without recent direct linkage. Geopolitical category moderately weighted.

ai_positioning.summary: The company PRGS does not explicitly mention artificial intelligence (AI) or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F report. The information provided focuses primarily on financial aspects, acquisitions, and details on convertible notes, without direct reference to AI.
